chapter.title: Scope
chapter.para: This specification defines a layered protocol stack that enables any ONVIF-compliant client to discover, configure, and consume data from any AI-enabled ONVIF-compliant device. The stack combines three open technologies:

listitem.para: ONVIF, for standardised device control;
MCP (Model Context Protocol), for standardised AI tool invocation and metadata streaming;
LinkML, for defining, validating, and sharing structured metadata schemas.

chapter.para: The document is divided into the following sections:
Scope: Defines the applicability and boundaries of this specification.
Building Blocks: Introduces the four constituent technologies — ONVIF, MCP, LinkML, and JSON-LD — and their individual roles in the stack.
Protocol Stack Architecture: Describes the overall layered architecture, the two buses, and the shared identity authority.
Service Discovery and Data Exchange: Defines the message sequences for connection establishment, schema retrieval, skill invocation, and metadata event delivery.
Authentication and Authorization: Specifies the JWT-based security model, ONVIF role mapping, and TLS requirements.

chapter.title: Overview
chapter.para: AI configurations are handled through the ai service. AI configurations are used to configure and control the intelligent functions as defined in this specification. The device provides AI configuration through the AI service. WSDL for this service is specified in http://www.onvif.org/ver20/media/wsdl/media.wsdll.

section.title: MCP — The AI Tool Interface
section.para: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open, JSON-RPC 2.0 based protocol designed to connect AI language models and agents to external tools and data sources. In the ONVIF AI stack, MCP serves as the standardised interface layer between the ONVIF Client (acting as an MCP Host) and each ONVIF Device (acting as an MCP Server). Adopting MCP means that any ONVIF Client can invoke any compliant ONVIF Device without requiring a vendor-specific driver.

section.title: Protocol Primitives
section.para: MCP defines three categories of server-side object that a host may discover and use:

listitem.para: Tools are callable operations with a named identifier, a human-readable description, and an inputSchema (JSON Schema) that fully describes the expected arguments. In the ONVIF AI stack, Tools are called Skills and represent ONVIF Device capabilities such as configuring a detection region or querying service status. The ONVIF Client invokes a Skill by sending a tools/call JSON-RPC request over the Control Bus.

Resources are read-only data objects accessible via resources/list and resources/read requests. In this specification, Resources carry the LinkML schema bundles that describe the event payloads and skill input parameters of the ONVIF Device. Each schema resource carries the MIME type application/linkml+yaml.
Prompts are optional server-defined interaction templates. This specification does not mandate Prompt support; ONVIF Devices MAY expose Prompts for human-in-the-loop workflows.

section.title: Transport Modes
section.para: This specification normatively uses the Streamable HTTP transport. The ONVIF Client sends JSON-RPC requests as HTTP POST to the ONVIF Device's /mcp endpoint. For server-initiated messages (schema update notifications, metadata events) the ONVIF Client also opens a long-lived HTTP GET on /mcp; the ONVIF Device sends newline-delimited JSON-RPC notifications over this persistent channel. An ONVIF Device conforming to this specification shall support the Streamable HTTP transport.

section.title: Protocol Version
section.para: This specification normatively requires MCP 2026-07-28. Implementations conforming to this specification shall not use the session-era MCP 2025-11-25 protocol.

MCP 2026-07-28 is a fully stateless protocol. There is no session establishment handshake and no Mcp-Session-Id header. Every HTTP request is self-contained: the ONVIF Client includes the MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28 request header on each call, together with the Authorization: Bearer JWT header. The ONVIF Device shall reject requests that carry a protocol version other than 2026-07-28 with HTTP 400.

Service discovery uses the server/discover JSON-RPC method, which replaces the initialize / initialized handshake of earlier versions. The response carries the server's capability flags (tools, resources, prompts) and its human-readable identity. As required by MCP 2026-07-28, the ONVIF Device shall implement server/discover. The ONVIF Client may call server/discover before issuing other requests to learn supported versions and capabilities, but it is not required to call it first and may invoke any operation directly and handle UnsupportedProtocolVersionError.

The stateless model is the correct choice for the ONVIF AI use case: ONVIF Devices are deployed as horizontally-scalable endpoints behind load balancers, and pinning a ONVIF Client to a specific server instance via a session identifier would prevent transparent failover and scaling. With MCP 2026-07-28, every request can be routed to any instance of the ONVIF Device without loss of state.

section.title: LinkML — Schema Definition Language
section.para: LinkML (Linked data Modeling Language) is an open schema definition language that describes data structures in YAML. In the ONVIF AI stack, LinkML is the normative language for defining both the structure of metadata events (Data Bus payloads) and the argument shapes of Skills (Control Bus inputs). LinkML defines the schema; JSON-LD (see ) is the runtime wire format that carries instances of that schema.

section.title: Schema Structure
section.para: A LinkML schema document is a YAML file with the following top-level keys:

listitem.para: id: a globally unique URI that serves as the schema identifier. This URI is reused as the JSON-LD @context value in every event payload emitted by the ONVIF Device, making the schema self-locating.

imports: a list of schema URIs from which common types are inherited. ONVIF maintains a shared type library (ver10_schema_common_linkml) that defines reusable structures such as bounding boxes, polygon regions, timestamps, and confidence scores. ONVIF Devices SHOULD import this library rather than redefining common types.

classes: named data structures with typed attributes, optional range constraints (minimum_value, maximum_value), and documentation strings. The root event class shall extend BaseAnalyticsEvent from the ONVIF common type library.
enums: closed value sets used for categorical fields such as SeverityLevel (low, medium, high, critical) and event type discriminators.

section.title: Dual Role: Event Schema and Skill Input Schema
section.para: The same LinkML model serves two distinct purposes within the stack:

listitem.para: On the Data Bus, the compiled JSON Schema derived from the LinkML model is used by the ONVIF Client LinkML Validator (Layer 2) to check every incoming metadata event for structural correctness — required fields, numeric ranges, and valid enum values.

On the Control Bus, the inputSchema field of each MCP Tool (Skill) definition is also derived from the same LinkML model. This guarantees that the coordinate spaces, unit definitions, and vocabulary used to configure the ONVIF Device (e.g., a detection region polygon) are identical to those used to report events, eliminating a class of integration errors that arise when configuration and reporting use incompatible data models.

section.title: Compilation to JSON Schema
section.para: The LinkML toolchain provides a generator that produces a JSON Schema document from a LinkML YAML source. This compiled JSON Schema is used in two places:

listitem.para: First, it is embedded in the inputSchema field of each MCP Tool definition returned by tools/list. The ONVIF Client can validate skill arguments against this schema before sending a tools/call request, providing early client-side error detection.

Second, a copy of the compiled schema is stored in the ONVIF Client Schema Registry (Layer 2) after schema discovery. The registry uses the compiled schema to validate every incoming metadata event on the Data Bus before the ONVIF Client processes it.

section.para: ONVIF Devices shall pre-compile their LinkML schemas at build time and include the compiled JSON Schema in Tool definitions. The source YAML shall also be exposed as a schema Resource so that the ONVIF Client can re-compile or audit the schema independently.

section.title: ONVIF Common Type Library
section.para: The ONVIF AI Working Group maintains a shared LinkML type library (ver10_schema_common_linkml) that defines base classes and enumerations used across all ONVIF Devices. Key types include:

BaseAnalyticsEvent: the mandatory root class for all metadata events, defining the required fields event_id (UUID), timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC), source_uri, confidence (float, 0.0–1.0), and severity (SeverityLevel enum).
BoundingBox and PolygonRegion: normalised coordinate structures shared between event payloads and skill input schemas to ensure consistent spatial referencing.

ONVIF shall not redefine any type declared in the common type library. This ensures that an ONVIF Client that has already loaded the common library does not need to re-fetch it for each new ONVIF Device it connects to.

section.title: JSON-LD — Wire Format for Metadata Events
section.para: JSON-LD (JSON-based Linked Data) is the serialisation format used for all metadata events transmitted on the Data Bus. Where LinkML defines the schema at design time, JSON-LD carries instances of that schema at runtime. The two technologies are complementary: LinkML declares what data looks like; JSON-LD is the payload that conforms to that declaration.

section.title: Context and Type Annotations
section.para: Every metadata event emitted by an ONVIF Device shall include two mandatory JSON-LD keywords:

@context: a URI that points to the canonical LinkML schema for this event type. The value shall equal the id field of the LinkML schema from which the event class is derived. This URI is the primary key used by the ONVIF Client Schema Registry to look up the compiled JSON Schema for validation.

@type: the class name of the event as declared in the LinkML schema (e.g., FireDetectionEvent, PersonCrossingEvent). This field allows the ONVIF Client to route the event to the appropriate handler without inspecting the full payload.

Together, @context and @type make each event self-describing: an ONVIF Client that receives an event with an unfamiliar @context URI knows exactly where to fetch the schema needed to understand and validate the event.

section.title: Self-Describing Events and Dynamic Schema Registration
section.para: The self-describing nature of JSON-LD enables a dynamic schema registration workflow. When the ONVIF Client Schema Registry (Layer 2) receives a metadata event whose @context URI does not match any registered schema, it SHOULD:
1. Suspend validation of the triggering event.
2. Fetch the LinkML schema YAML from the URI identified by @context, or issue an MCP resources/read request to the originating ONVIF Device to retrieve the latest schema bundle.
3. Register the schema bundle in the local registry.
4. Re-validate and process the suspended event against the newly registered schema.

This mechanism allows an ONVIF Device to introduce a new event type (e.g., a firmware update that adds a VehicleTypeDetectionEvent) without requiring a pre-coordinated ONVIF Client update. The ONVIF Client self-heals its schema knowledge at runtime.

section.title: Relationship to Linked Data
section.para: Although full JSON-LD processing (graph expansion, context dereferencing, SPARQL querying) is not required by this specification, the use of JSON-LD framing ensures forward compatibility with semantic web tooling. A conformant ONVIF Client shall treat @context and @type as opaque identifiers for schema lookup and event routing. An ONVIF Client MAY additionally perform full JSON-LD processing for downstream applications such as knowledge graph ingestion or cross-vendor event correlation.

section.title: Architecture Overview
section.para: The ONVIF AI Protocol Stack is structured around the standard ONVIF roles of an ONVIF Client and an ONVIF Device, with an OIDC Authorization Server acting as the shared trust anchor that issues the tokens consumed by both. The figure below shows the top-level relationships between these three components and the two communication buses.

figure.title: ONVIF AI Protocol Stack — Top-Level Architecture

section.para: The OIDC Authorization Server is the trust anchor for the entire stack. It issues signed ES256 JWTs to the ONVIF Client via the OAuth2 Client Credentials grant, and exposes a JWKS endpoint that the ONVIF Device uses to validate every token it receives.

The ONVIF Client combines the ONVIF Client role with the MCP Host role. It manages connections to ONVIF Devices, invokes skills, and subscribes to metadata events. It also maintains the LinkML Schema Registry and validates every incoming event before it is passed to business logic.

The ONVIF Device provides an MCP Server endpoint. Through this endpoint, it exposes skills in the form of MCP Tools and publishes JSON-LD metadata events. Moreover, it announces the LinkML schema via MCP Resources.

All communication between the ONVIF Client and the ONVIF Device is bearer-token authenticated. The Control Bus (A) carries MCP tools/call requests from the ONVIF Client to the ONVIF Device. The Data Bus (B) carries JSON-LD metadata events from the ONVIF Device to the ONVIF Client, delivered as MCP notifications/message frames.

section.title: Protocol Stack
section.para: The ONVIF AI protocol stack uses two independent communication buses, both protected by TLS and bearer tokens issued by the OIDC Authorization Server. The Control Bus carries client-initiated MCP requests, while the Data Bus carries server-pushed metadata events. The detailed behavior of each bus is defined in the following sections.

section.title: Control Bus
section.para: The Control Bus is the command path used by the ONVIF Client to discover and invoke Skills exposed by an ONVIF Device. It is request/response oriented and carries only client-initiated MCP operations.

entry.para: Discover capabilities, list skills, and invoke device actions.
HTTP POST to /mcp over HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2.
server/discover, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, and resources/read.
TLS 1.3 with an Authorization: Bearer ES256 JWT on every request.

section.para: Each request is self-contained and shall be validated independently by the ONVIF Device before execution. A Control Bus response shall report either the requested result or an MCP error indicating why the operation could not be completed.

section.title: Metadata Data Bus
section.para: The Metadata Data Bus is the event path used by the ONVIF Device to publish AI analytics results to the ONVIF Client. It is server-initiated, asynchronous, and optimized for continuous delivery of structured metadata events.

entry.para: Deliver detection and analytics events as they occur.
MCP 2026-07-28 over Streamable HTTP persistent GET.
HTTP GET to /mcp over HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2.
JSON-LD events conforming to the registered LinkML schema.
TLS 1.3 with an Authorization: Bearer ES256 JWT on every request.

section.para: The Data Bus shall preserve event ordering per stream, and each event shall remain self-describing through its JSON-LD @context and @type annotations.

section.title: Identity and Authorization Server
section.para: The ONVIF AI protocol stack requires an OAuth 2.1 Authorization Server, as specified in the ONVIF Security Service Specification.

This server acts as the trust anchor for the complete stack: it authenticates clients, issues bearer access tokens, and exposes the metadata and key material needed by ONVIF Devices to validate tokens before processing MCP requests.

In practice, the Authorization Server provides centralized identity and access control for both buses. It ensures that only authorized ONVIF Clients can invoke Skills on the Control Bus and receive protected metadata on the Data Bus, according to the roles and claims contained in the issued token.

section.title: Network Discovery
section.para: MCP 2026-07-28 does not define network-level device discovery. Therefore, ONVIF Device discovery remains dependent on the mechanisms specified by [ONVIF Core]. An ONVIF Client shall discover ONVIF Devices and obtain their service endpoint using the ONVIF Core discovery procedures before initiating MCP requests.

section.title: Service Discovery
section.para: An ONVIF Device that supports the AI Service shall advertise the MCP service endpoint URL through the ONVIF Core service discovery mechanism. In the ONVIF Core GetServices response, the corresponding AI Service entry (tds:GetServiceResponse) shall contain the service address used by the ONVIF Client for MCP requests.

section.title: Capability Discovery
section.para: Capability discovery shall be performed through the MCP resources/read operation using the resource URI capabilities://onvif/ai.

An ONVIF Device implementing the AI Service shall expose capabilities://onvif/ai and shall return the AI Service capabilities through resources/read. Exposing capabilities for other ONVIF services is optional; when provided, the same URI pattern shall be used by replacing ai with the service name (for example, capabilities://onvif/<service-name>).

chapter.title: Authentication and Authorization
chapter.para: The ONVIF AI protocol stack delegates all authentication and token management to the mechanisms defined in the ONVIF Core Specification and the ONVIF Security Service Specification. Those documents govern JWT token format and required claims (iss, aud, exp, nbf, roles), the mandatory ES256 signing algorithm, token validation rules, the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow, authorization server configuration, and TLS transport requirements. Implementations not comply with the ONVIF Core Specification and the ONVIF Security Service Specification. This chapter defines only the ONVIF AI-specific normative mapping of MCP operations to ONVIF access classes.

section.title: Role-to-MCP Operation Mapping
section.para: The ONVIF Security Service Specification defines three predefined JWT role values carried in the roles claim of every access token: onvif:User, onvif:Operator, and onvif:Administrator. These correspond to the ONVIF user levels and cover the majority of deployments. For environments that require finer-grained access control, the Security Service Specification defines a full user role management model that allows custom roles to be assigned to individual users; refer to the ONVIF Security Service Specification for details. The onvif: namespace prefix is reserved; custom roles shall not use it.

Anonymous access to any MCP endpoint is not permitted. Every request to the ONVIF Device shall carry a valid Authorization: Bearer JWT. The ONVIF Device maps the access class required by each MCP operation against the roles claim in the presented token and rejects requests that do not satisfy the minimum role requirement with HTTP 403. A token carrying onvif:Administrator satisfies all lower access class requirements; a token carrying onvif:Operator satisfies READ_SYSTEM in addition to ACTUATE.
The table below is normative. Each Skill exposed via tools/list shall include an annotation declaring its access class. The ONVIF Device shall enforce this mapping at runtime.

chapter.title: Metadata
chapter.para: This chapter defines the data model for structured metadata produced and consumed by ONVIF AI-enabled devices. All metadata payloads are instances of, or derived from, the abstract classes defined here. The normative schema is expressed in LinkML; JSON-LD is the wire format (see ).

section.title: Observation
section.para: Observation is the top-level abstract container for every piece of information emitted by an ONVIF AI Device. Because AI services produce heterogeneous outputs — object detection results, fire alerts, people counts, anomaly reports — the class is intentionally abstract: domain-specific event classes derive from it and add their own semantic fields. An ONVIF Device shall serialise every AI metadata payload as an instance of a class that directly or transitively extends Observation.

Every Observation instance carries a mandatory unique identifier and a creation timestamp. Three optional nested objects — Provenance, Location, and Timing — provide contextual metadata about authenticity, spatial origin, and temporal reference respectively. Each is defined by an abstract class; concrete implementations are described in the following sections.

section.title: SOSAObservation
section.para: SOSAObservation is the first concrete subclass of Observation defined by this specification. It aligns the ONVIF AI metadata model with the W3C Semantic Sensor Network (SSN) / SOSA ontology (https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-ssn/), enabling interoperability with the broader Linked Data and IoT ecosystem.

SOSA defines an Observation as an act carried out by a Sensor that produces a Result whose value estimates or calculates a value of an ObservableProperty of a FeatureOfInterest. The SOSAObservation class maps these four SOSA roles directly to ONVIF AI Device semantics:

listitem.para: madeBySensor — the ONVIF AI component (camera, analytics module, or AI inference engine) that produced the observation. Corresponds to sosa:madeBySensor.
observedProperty — the physical or logical property being measured or inferred (for example onvif:PersonCount, onvif:FlamePresence). Corresponds to sosa:observedProperty.
hasFeatureOfInterest — the real-world entity about which the observation is made (for example a scene, a zone, or a specific object). Corresponds to sosa:hasFeatureOfInterest.
hasResult — the value or structured object that is the outcome of the observation (for example a count, a bounding box, or a probability score). Corresponds to sosa:hasResult.

phenomenonTime — the time interval or instant during which the observed property held the reported value. Distinct from the observation creation timestamp inherited from Observation. Corresponds to sosa:phenomenonTime.
resultTime — the instant at which the result became available (the observation was completed). Corresponds to sosa:resultTime.
usedProcedure — the AI algorithm or procedure applied by the sensor to produce the result (optional). Corresponds to sosa:usedProcedure.

section.para: All four mandatory fields (madeBySensor, observedProperty, hasFeatureOfInterest, and hasResult) shall be present in every serialised SOSAObservation instance. The ONVIF AI Device shall use sosa: URIs as JSON-LD property keys to ensure full alignment with the SOSA ontology.

section.title: Provenance
section.para: Provenance is an abstract class nested within Observation that describes the authenticity and chain-of-custody of the observation. Because different deployment environments require different attestation mechanisms — cryptographic signatures, hash-of-source-frame, hardware attestation tokens, or simple device identity — the class is abstract and shall be specialised for each mechanism. Concrete subclasses add the fields specific to their attestation method.
The presence of a Provenance object is optional. When omitted, no authenticity claim is made for the observation.

section.title: JLDSProvenance
section.para: JLDSProvenance is the first concrete subclass of Provenance. It attests the integrity of an Observation by means of a JSON-LD Data Integrity proof [VC-DATA-INTEGRITY]. The ECC signature algorithm and key parameters shall conform to the ONVIF Security Baseline [ONVIF-SecurityBaseline].

section.title: Signing procedure
section.para: The ONVIF Device shall compute the proof using the Add Proof algorithm defined in [VC-DATA-INTEGRITY] with RDFC-1.0 [RDFC-1.0] as the canonicalization algorithm. The digest and signing algorithms shall be those mandated by the current version of [ONVIF-SecurityBaseline].

section.title: Proof fields
section.para: JLDSProvenance carries the following fields, aligned with the DataIntegrityProof structure defined in [VC-DATA-INTEGRITY]:

listitem.para: type (mandatory) — fixed string "DataIntegrityProof".

cryptosuite (mandatory) — identifies the cryptosuite used. The value shall correspond to the algorithm profile mandated by the current version of [ONVIF-SecurityBaseline]. It is included in the proof configuration and therefore covered by the signature.
created (mandatory) — ISO 8601 UTC datetime at which the proof was created.
verificationMethod (mandatory) — URI of the public key or verification method that can be used to verify the proof.
proofPurpose (mandatory) — fixed string "assertionMethod".
proofValue (mandatory) — the encoded digital signature over hashData as defined in the signing procedure above.

section.title: Location
section.para: Location is an abstract class nested within Observation that represents the spatial origin of the observation. It is optional; when present it shall be an instance of a concrete subclass.

section.title: GeoLocation
section.para: GeoLocation is the first concrete subclass of Location. It expresses geographic position using WGS 84 coordinates obtained from a GPS receiver integrated in, or connected to, the ONVIF Device. It carries latitude and longitude as mandatory fields and an optional altitude above mean sea level.

section.title: Timing
section.para: Timing is an abstract class nested within Observation that provides an authoritative time reference for the observation, independent of the device system clock. It is optional; when present it shall be an instance of a concrete subclass.

section.title: GPSTiming
section.para: GPSTiming is the first concrete subclass of Timing. It carries the UTC timestamp extracted directly from the GPS signal, giving a traceable, drift-free time reference. An optional UTC offset field allows representation of local time where required.

section.title: Normative LinkML Schema
section.para: This section is here just because it is handy now, it will be removed before releasing the specs.

The following LinkML YAML fragment is normative. All abstract classes are marked abstract: true; concrete subclasses set is_a to their parent. Fields marked required: true shall be present in every serialised instance; all other fields are optional.

Observation: abstract: true description: >- Top-level abstract container for every AI metadata payload emitted by an ONVIF Device. Domain-specific event classes shall extend this class. attributes: id: range: uriorcurie required: true description: Globally unique identifier for this observation instance. timestamp: range: datetime required: true description: >- Creation time of the observation, expressed as an ISO 8601 datetime in UTC. provenance: range: Provenance required: false description: >- Authenticity and chain-of-custody descriptor. Omitted when no attestation claim is made. location: range: Location required: false description: Spatial origin of the observation. timing: range: Timing required: false description: Authoritative time reference for the observation.

GeoLocation: is_a: Location description: >- WGS 84 geographic position obtained from a GPS receiver attached to or integrated in the ONVIF Device. attributes: latitude: range: double required: true minimum_value: -90.0 maximum_value: 90.0 description: Geodetic latitude in decimal degrees (WGS 84). longitude: range: double required: true minimum_value: -180.0 maximum_value: 180.0 description: Geodetic longitude in decimal degrees (WGS 84). altitude: range: double required: false description: Altitude above mean sea level in metres (WGS 84).
Timing: abstract: true description: >- Abstract authoritative time reference for an Observation, independent of the device system clock. Concrete subclasses specify the time source.

Informative only.
JLDSProvenance: is_a: Provenance description: >- Concrete Provenance subclass that attests Observation integrity using a JSON-LD Data Integrity proof [VC-DATA-INTEGRITY]. The ECC signature algorithm and key parameters shall conform to [ONVIF-SecurityBaseline]. The proof is computed over the RDFC-1.0 canonical form of the Observation with the provenance field excluded. attributes: type: range: string required: true equals_string: "DataIntegrityProof" description: >- Fixed value "DataIntegrityProof" as defined in [VC-DATA-INTEGRITY]. cryptosuite: range: string required: true description: >- Identifies the cryptosuite used. The value shall be consistent with the ECC algorithm mandated by [ONVIF-SecurityBaseline]. created: range: datetime required: true description: ISO 8601 UTC datetime at which the proof was created. verificationMethod: range: uriorcurie required: true description: >- URI of the public key or verification method used to verify the proof. proofPurpose: range: string required: true equals_string: "assertionMethod" description: >- Fixed value "assertionMethod", indicating the proof asserts the content of the observation. proofValue: range: string required: true description: >- Encoded digital signature over hashData = H(canonical(unsecuredDocument)) || H(canonical(proofConfig)), where unsecuredDocument is the Observation with provenance removed, proofConfig is the proof object without proofValue, and H and the signing algorithm are mandated by [ONVIF-SecurityBaseline].
SOSAObservation: is_a: Observation description: >- Concrete Observation subclass aligned with the W3C SOSA ontology (https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-ssn/). Instances shall be serialised using sosa: property URIs as JSON-LD keys. class_uri: sosa:Observation attributes: madeBySensor: slot_uri: sosa:madeBySensor range: uriorcurie required: true description: >- URI identifying the ONVIF AI component (camera, analytics module, or inference engine) that produced this observation. observedProperty: slot_uri: sosa:observedProperty range: uriorcurie required: true description: >- URI identifying the physical or logical property being measured or inferred (e.g. onvif:PersonCount, onvif:FlamePresence). hasFeatureOfInterest: slot_uri: sosa:hasFeatureOfInterest range: uriorcurie required: true description: >- URI identifying the real-world entity about which the observation is made (e.g. a scene, a detection zone, or a specific object). hasResult: slot_uri: sosa:hasResult range: Any required: true description: >- The result value or structured object produced by the observation (e.g. a count, a bounding box, or a probability score). phenomenonTime: slot_uri: sosa:phenomenonTime range: datetime required: false description: >- The time instant or interval during which the observed property held the reported value. May differ from the Observation timestamp. resultTime: slot_uri: sosa:resultTime range: datetime required: false description: >- The instant at which the result became available (observation completed). Corresponds to sosa:resultTime. usedProcedure: slot_uri: sosa:usedProcedure range: uriorcurie required: false description: >- URI identifying the AI algorithm or procedure applied by the sensor to produce the result.

appendix.title: Example Call Sequence (informative)
appendix.para: This annex is informative and provides an example end-to-end sequence with sample values.

section.title: Network discovery (ONVIF Core)
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends ONVIF Core discovery requests (for example WS-Discovery Probe) to locate devices on the network.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns discovery responses (for example ProbeMatches) with the Device Service endpoint.

section.title: Service discovery (ONVIF Core GetServices)
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls ONVIF Core GetServices on the Device Service endpoint.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns GetServiceResponse including the AI Service entry with MCP endpoint URL (example: https://192.0.2.10/mcp).

section.title: Optional protocol preflight
section.para: Request (Client to Device): For MCP 2026-07-28, the ONVIF Client may call server/discover before other requests.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns service identity, supported protocol versions, and capability flags, or UnsupportedProtocolVersionError with the supported versions list.
Legacy example (informative only): For legacy MCP clients, an initialize request may be used.

para.emphasis: Legacy response (Device to Client, informative only):

section.title: AI capability discovery
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends resources/read with URI capabilities://onvif/ai.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns the AI Service capabilities document.

section.title: Optional non-AI capability discovery
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends resources/read with URI capabilities://onvif/<service-name> (example: capabilities://onvif/media).
Response (Device to Client): If supported, the ONVIF Device returns capabilities for the requested service; otherwise it returns a resource-not-found error.

section.title: Schema resource inventory
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends resources/list.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns available schema resources (example URIs: linkml://onvif/ai/events/v1, linkml://onvif/ai/skills/v1).

section.title: Schema retrieval
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends resources/read for each schema URI from resources/list (example: linkml://onvif/ai/events/v1).
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns schema content for each requested resource.

section.title: Tool discovery
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends tools/list.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns Skill definitions and input schemas (for example get_status, set_detection_region, set_sensitivity).

section.title: Skill invocation (read)
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends tools/call with name: "get_status" and arguments {}.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns current status as structured result content.

section.title: Skill invocation (actuate)
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends tools/call with name: "set_sensitivity" and sample arguments {"channel":"ch1","value":0.70}.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns operation outcome (success or authorization/validation error).

section.title: Metadata stream subscription
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client opens the persistent Streamable HTTP channel (GET https://192.0.2.10/mcp).
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device streams server-initiated notifications and JSON-LD metadata events on that channel.
